name: Corp City
mainDescription: Corp City is a city management game in which you run a city like a corporation. You have to manage your employee's wages and benefits budgets and upgrade the facilities of each sector to reach a certain profit quota every 5 years.
WorkSummary: For this project I designed and programmed and did the art for the UI. Because the UI is the only way the player interacts with the game, my UI programming ended up becoming the gameplay programming. The systems programming for this project was done by one of the other programmers as they also designed the systems.
HighlightTitle: Serving the narrative through UI Design
HighlightDescription: You'll notice the UI for this game doesn't look very pretty, being rigid, monochrome squares. This is to serve the game's narrative of being the CEO of the soulless corporation that controls the city. The conrast between the UI's drab lifelessness and the city's neon, exciting color scheme serves to illustrate the divide between the corporation that runs this city and the people that live in it.

name: Treekeeper
mainDescription: Treekeeper is a top-down tower defense shooter in which you defend The Great Tree from the fires of industry. Dash around the battlefield while placing towers or walls, then attack bots directly with your magic!
WorkSummary: I designed and programmed all of the UI in the game. I created a dynamic radial layout group script, modified my previously existing button rebinding system to be more modular(it can now more easily be slotted into future projects), and designed a dynamic gameplay UI system to address the issue of keeping the player informed but still aware of the battlefield.
HighlightDescription: For Treekeeper, we needed a way to have the player manage towers(Ents) but still able to quickly respond to threats without interrupting the flow of the game by pausing time, so the gameplay designers and I settled on the idea of each Ent having a context menu that pops up when you click on them to manage them. To make the radial layout it employs, I created a dynamic radial layout group script, a variation of Unity's native grid layout system that takes in a radius, start angle, and end angle, and automatically spaces and sizes each element.

name: Galax 2025
mainDescription: Galax 2025 is an unofficial remake of a 1988 game for MacOS called Galax. Conquer the galaxy one planet at a time in this space strategy game! Play the original way against the Gubru and the Czin or play against a friend in pass & play mode!
WorkSummary: I played the original through an emulator until I was able to figure out how the game worked, then remade it in Unity as best I could.
HighlightTitle: Remaking a game my father remembered
HighlightDescription: Galax 2025 was a project I undertook to recreate a game my father had played when he was around my age. this meant studying the original through an emulator and his original copy of the game from 1988, as Galax was so obscure that it wasn't even on the internet archive until my father uploaded it. I, with the help of my father's recollection of the game, remade it in Unity, though it's not quite a 1 to 1 remake as my version allows for pass & play multiplayer, in addition to some of the math not being exactly what it was in the original, but my best approximation from testing the results. Every sprite and graphic I recreated in Aseprite, every systems I programmed to get as close to the feel of the original as I could.

name: Kaleido
mainDescription: Kaleido will be a JRPG with fighting game elements about a hue named Gray as they go on a journey of self-discovery across the continent of Kaleido, finding their artistic style and making many friends along the way.
WorkSummary: I joined this project in February 2024, and then development paused in August of that year. We started development again in October 2025, and I threw out most of my old work as I am a much more proficient developer now. Additionally, development has been slow as our team is all still in college and have been contributing small amounts whenever we have time between classes.
HighlightDescription: My main work for Kaleido that I can show off is the overworld UI. This image is the current mockup of the inventory screen, but I will be remaking most of this as we have decided to go another direction for the aesthetic of the overworld menus. I had made a party management system, though I have scrapped most of it and am in the process of making a better version.
